newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Italy, Kuwait seek long-term cooperation - agency.
newsitem.headline: Italy, Kuwait seek long-term cooperation - agency.

text.p: Italy and Kuwait agreed on Thursday to form a joint committee to map long-term cooperation, the official Kuwait News Agency reported.
"Italian Prime Minister (Romano Prodi) said he had accepted a proposal by Kuwait to form a joint committee...to follow up issues of mutual interest," it said.
"The committee will lay a policy for long-term cooperation," said Prodi, at the end of a visit to Kuwait meant to boost ties between the two countries mainly in the area of economy.
Prodi "said his talks with the Kuwaiti side tackled boosting cooperation in industrial and military areas," the agency said.

Kuwait's imports from Italy rose 23 percent in 1995 to about $380 million, and 15 percent in the nine months to September 1996. Kuwait's exports to Italy stood at about $10 million in 1995. No comparative figures were available.
Italy's exports to Kuwait are mainly machinery for the oil industry, clothes and leather products.

Prodi met the country's Emir Sheikh Jaber al-Ahmad al-Sabah and acting Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sheikh Sabah al-Ahmad al-Sabah. He was accompanied by 15 businessmen, mainly oil and energy industrialists.

Italy participated in the 1991 U.S.-led offensive that drove Iraqi troops from Kuwait after a seven-month occupation. Prodi said Iraq must obey all Security Council resolutions before sanctions can be eased. Baghdad has been under a strict U.N. trade embargo since its occupation of Kuwait.
